submission.clinical_question: What is the cause of secondary amenorrhea in this 32-year-old female with history of D&C for missed abortion and CIN 3?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32-year-old female with six-month history of secondary amenorrhea and intermittent pelvic pain. History significant for cervical conization with LEEP (18 months ago), D&C for missed abortion (1 year ago), and vaginal delivery with episiotomy (6 months ago). Hormonal workup is normal (FSH, LH, prolactin, TSH within normal limits; beta-hCG negative). Physical exam shows normal-sized uterus with no adnexal masses. Hysterosalpingogram demonstrates filling defect in the uterine cavity with scant passage of contrast into proximal fallopian tubes, suggestive of intrauterine pathology.
must_include_findings: filling defect in the uterine cavity
scant passage of contrast material into proximal fallopian tubes

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of acute ischemic stroke in this patient presenting with sudden onset right-sided numbness?
submission.pre_read_summary: 70-year-old male with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and degenerative conduction system disease presents to ED with sudden onset numbness on the right side of his face, arm, and leg without weakness, slurred speech, or visual changes. Physical exam demonstrates decreased pinprick, vibration, and proprioception over the entire right side of his body and face. Family history significant for father's ischemic stroke at age 74. Patient is on aspirin, metformin, lisinopril, amlodipine, and atorvastatin. Initial imaging already noted a small lacunar infarct.
must_include_findings: No mass effect or midline shift

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of recurrent lung abscess or pulmonary infection in a patient with chronic aspiration risk and history of tuberculosis?
submission.pre_read_summary: 53M with severe alcohol use disorder and chronic aspiration risk presents with 3-week history of fever, night sweats, productive cough with foul-smelling sputum, and 10-pound weight loss. Physical exam reveals decreased breath sounds with dullness to percussion at right lung base. Labs show leukocytosis (WBC 15,000/µL). History includes treated tuberculosis (2022-03-15), prior lung abscess (2022-09-15) with Bacteroides spp growth, and recurrent aspiration events. Previous imaging demonstrated cavitary lesion with air-fluid level in right lower lobe. Current imaging ordered to evaluate for recurrent pulmonary infection/abscess.
must_include_findings: cavitary lesion in right lower lobe

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of hematocolpos causing severe lower abdominal pain in a 15-year-old female with known imperforate hymen?
submission.pre_read_summary: 15-year-old female with known imperforate hymen and hematocolpos presenting with severe acute lower abdominal pain and difficulty with defecation for 6 hours and 2 days respectively. Patient has complex history including primary amenorrhea, androgen insensitivity syndrome, and 5-alpha reductase deficiency. Physical exam reveals distended lower abdomen with suprapubic tenderness and bulging bluish membrane at vaginal introitus. Previous imaging (2020) showed no uterus or ovaries, but most recent ultrasound (this encounter) shows distended vagina filled with fluid and normal uterus. No renal anomalies noted.
must_include_findings: bulging membrane at vaginal introitus on physical exam

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of deep vein thrombosis in the left lower extremity?
submission.pre_read_summary: 9-year-old male with known homocystinuria and history of lower extremity DVT presents with acute-onset left leg swelling and pain that began 2 days ago. Physical examination reveals left leg tenderness and edema. Patient is on pyridoxine, betaine anhydrous, folic acid, and aspirin for homocystinuria management. No history of trauma, surgery, or immobilization.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of additional thoracic injuries (rib fractures, hemothorax, pulmonary contusion, or other complications) beyond the known right clavicular fracture and small right-sided pneumothorax in this patient with bicycle accident trauma?
submission.pre_read_summary: 28-year-old male presents to the emergency department after a bicycle accident. He was wearing a helmet and did not lose consciousness, but reports falling onto his right side and striking his shoulder against the curb. Chief complaint is pain in right shoulder and difficulty breathing. Physical exam reveals tenderness over the right clavicle and decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. Initial chest x-ray has already identified a right clavicular fracture and small right-sided pneumothorax. No rib fractures or hemothorax were initially seen. Patient is hemodynamically stable. Past medical history is unremarkable.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of recurrent herpes simplex encephalitis or other intracranial pathology in this patient with fever, headache, confusion, and new-onset seizures?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32-year-old female with known history of herpes simplex encephalitis (diagnosed 2020-01-15) presenting with two-day history of fever (38.9°C), headache, confusion, and two episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Physical exam reveals hyperreflexia and positive right Babinski sign. CSF analysis shows pleocytosis (150 WBC/mm³, 90% lymphocytes), elevated protein (100 mg/dL), and normal glucose ratio. Previous MRI (not yet reviewed in detail) showed increased T2 signal in left temporal lobe with edema. Current urgent CT shows no hemorrhage or mass effect. MRI of head ordered to evaluate for recurrent encephalitis or other intracranial pathology.
must_include_findings: T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in temporal lobes (especially left)
any mass effect or midline shift

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pulmonary edema and heart failure exacerbation?
submission.pre_read_summary: 67-year-old male with known heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 30%), polycythemia vera, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea requiring 3 pillows, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam reveals jugular venous distension, bibasilar crackles, S3 gallop, and mild bilateral ankle edema. BNP is elevated at 900 pg/mL. Previous imaging showed cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion. Current chest x-ray shows prominent pulmonary vessels and mild hazy opacities in lower lung fields.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of diaphragmatic hernia or other intrathoracic pathology explaining the patient's acute chest pain and shortness of breath?
submission.pre_read_summary: 35-year-old male presenting to ED with sudden onset shortness of breath and left-sided chest pain. Vitals: HR 105, RR 22, O2 sat 92% on room air. History of multiple traumatic rib fractures (healed), pulmonary contusion (resolved), and mild traumatic brain injury. Physical exam reveals decreased breath sounds and tympanic note to percussion over left hemithorax. Chest x-ray demonstrates elevated left hemidiaphragm with bowel loops in the left thoracic cavity and mediastinal shift to the right.
must_include_findings: bowel loops in left thoracic cavity

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of Meckel's diverticulum as the cause of GI bleeding in this 2-year-old male with intermittent abdominal pain and bloody stools?
submission.pre_read_summary: 2-year-old male with 6-month history of intermittent abdominal pain and recent onset of loose stools streaked with blood. Physical exam shows mild periumbilical tenderness with no palpable masses. Laboratory studies are normal (CBC, electrolytes, LFTs). Technetium-99m pertechnetate scan demonstrates uptake in an abnormal outpouching connected to the gastrointestinal tract, which is highly suggestive of Meckel's diverticulum containing ectopic gastric mucosa.
must_include_findings: Location and size of the abnormal outpouching
Uptake pattern on technetium-99m pertechnetate scan
Relationship of the outpouching to the gastrointestinal tract
Any associated inflammatory changes or complications

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of structural brain abnormalities (cortical tubers, subependymal nodules) consistent with tuberous sclerosis complex that may be contributing to the new onset seizures?
submission.pre_read_summary: 5-year-old male with new onset seizures characterized by sudden loss of consciousness and generalized convulsions, with associated school difficulties. Physical examination reveals hypopigmented ash-leaf-shaped patches on back and reddish papules on nasolabial folds. Family history significant for suspected X-linked chronic granulomatous disease in maternal uncles. Patient is on Levetiracetam 200 mg PO BID. EEG shows epileptiform discharges. MRI brain ordered to evaluate for structural abnormalities.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO) or other causes of respiratory distress in this 3-year-old post-blood transfusion?
submission.pre_read_summary: 3-year-old male with sickle-beta thalassemia and ALL presenting with acute respiratory distress and cough 4 hours after packed red blood cell transfusion for vaso-occlusive crisis. Patient is tachypneic (RR 40), tachycardic (HR 150), hypoxic (SpO2 88% on room air), with bilateral rales on lung auscultation. Labs show elevated BNP (580 pg/mL). Chest X-ray demonstrates pulmonary edema.

differential.diagnosis: Sickle cell crisis with pulmonary involvement

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pulmonary edema, pneumonia, or other acute cardiopulmonary pathology?
submission.pre_read_summary: 71-year-old male with known heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and CKD presents to ED with acute onset shortness of breath and productive cough with pink, frothy sputum. 2-week history of increasing lower extremity edema and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Vitals: RR 30, HR 110, O2 sat 88% on room air. Physical exam shows bilateral rales and elevated JVP. Labs: BNP 900 pg/mL, hypoxemia (PaO2 58). Previous CXR showed cardiomegaly with cephalization. Current CXR shows cardiomegaly and cephalization of pulmonary vasculature.

differential.diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of breast pathology (including malignancy) in a 42-year-old woman with left breast pain on tamoxifen therapy?
submission.pre_read_summary: 42-year-old female with a complex endocrine history including Hashimoto thyroiditis, Celiac disease, prolactinoma (treated with transsphenoidal resection), and primary adrenal insufficiency. Currently on multiple medications including Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for breast cancer prophylaxis/treatment, Cabergoline for prolactinoma, and thyroid/adrenal replacement. Presents with 3-month history of sharp left breast pain localized to the upper outer quadrant, not cyclical. Physical exam is unremarkable with no palpable masses, skin changes, or lymphadenopathy. Last mammogram 18 months ago was normal. No family history of breast cancer.
must_include_findings: Breast tissue evaluation for masses, calcifications, and architectural distortion
Comparison with prior mammogram from 18 months ago (reported normal)
Evaluation of left breast specifically given patient's complaint

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of nephrolithiasis or other pathology causing left flank pain?
submission.pre_read_summary: 50M with history of nephrolithiasis, gout, and type 2 diabetes presents with acute left flank pain for 2 days. Pain is sharp, radiates to groin, associated with nausea. Physical exam demonstrates left costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis shows uric acid crystals and elevated serum uric acid. Previous imaging identified 6 mm radiolucent stone in left ureter.
must_include_findings: 6 mm radiolucent stone in left ureter

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of a primary bone malignancy in the right distal femur causing the patient's progressive knee pain?
submission.pre_read_summary: 15M with 3 months of progressive right knee pain worsening at night and with physical activity, resulting in limp during basketball practice. Physical exam reveals firm tender mass over distal anterior thigh with mild warmth and decreased range of motion. Laboratory studies show elevated alkaline phosphatase and lactate dehydrogenase. Radiographs demonstrate destructive metaphyseal lesion with mixed radiodensity, periosteal new bone formation in "sunburst" pattern, and triangular elevation of periosteum (Codman's triangle). MRI confirms cortical destruction and soft-tissue mass. Biopsy reveals pleomorphic tumor cells producing osteoid.
must_include_findings: Destructive metaphyseal lesion with mixed radiodensity
Periosteal new bone formation in sunburst pattern
Pleomorphic tumor cells producing osteoid on biopsy

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of lymphoma given the patient's presentation of painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), pruritus, hepatomegaly, elevated LDH, and mediastinal widening?
submission.pre_read_summary: 17-year-old male with beta-thalassemia major and post-splenectomy status presents with a 6-week history of painless swelling in the left neck and supraclavicular area. He reports systemic B symptoms including persistent fatigue, night sweats, low-grade fevers, generalized pruritus (especially at night), and 10-pound weight loss over 2 months. Physical examination reveals a firm, rubbery, non-tender right supraclavicular lymph node (~3 cm), multiple enlarged anterior cervical and axillary lymph nodes, and hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, normal WBC, elevated ESR, and elevated LDH. Chest x-ray demonstrates widening of the superior mediastinum. A core biopsy of the right supraclavicular lymph node was performed. The constellation of painless lymphadenopathy, B symptoms, pruritus, elevated LDH, and mediastinal widening is highly concerning for lymphoma.
must_include_findings: multiple enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes
B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of bowel obstruction in this neonate with history of duodenal atresia repair presenting with persistent bilious vomiting?
submission.pre_read_summary: Newborn male with Trisomy 21 presenting with persistent bilious vomiting and mild upper abdominal distension. History of duodenal atresia repair (duodenoduodenostomy), Hirschsprung disease repair (Soave pull-through), and complete atrioventricular septal defect repair. Prenatal ultrasound showed polyhydramnios. Physical exam shows mildly distended upper abdomen with normal bowel sounds. Nasogastric tube yielded green fluid. No fever or abnormal vital signs.
must_include_findings: Evidence of bowel obstruction (dilated loops, air-fluid levels)
Double bubble sign or other signs of duodenal obstruction

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pneumonia?
submission.pre_read_summary: 37-year-old male with history of Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis and Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome presents to ICU with progressive fatigue, difficulty swallowing, and painful skin lesions following an urgent care visit for upper respiratory illness. Patient reports low-grade fevers, body aches, and has developed widespread skin lesions with blistering and peeling. Physical exam reveals Nikolsky sign positive, mucosal involvement (mouth, eyes, genitals), and febrile, tachycardic status. Labs show mild leukopenia and elevated liver enzymes. Chest radiograph was ordered to rule out pneumonia.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of mesenteric ischemia or bowel infarction in this 70M with recent AAA repair presenting with severe periumbilical pain?
submission.pre_read_summary: 70M with recent endovascular AAA repair (1 week ago) and complex vascular history (ischemic colitis, cholesterol embolism, arteriovenous fistula) presents with sudden onset severe periumbilical abdominal pain for 12 hours. Patient has tachycardia (HR 105), fever (37.8°C), elevated WBC (16,000), elevated lactate (5 mmol/L), and acute kidney injury (Cr 1.8 vs baseline 1.2). Physical exam shows distended abdomen with diffuse tenderness, guarding, and hypoactive bowel sounds. Prior CT (2022-01) showed intestinal obstruction. Current CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast shows bowel wall thickening and pneumatosis intestinalis, concerning for bowel ischemia/infarction.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of intra-abdominal injury (specifically splenic injury) following motor vehicle collision?
submission.pre_read_summary: 28-year-old male presents to ED following motor vehicle collision as restrained driver in car that hit a tree at moderate speed. Complains of left upper quadrant abdominal pain and dizziness. Vitals show tachycardia (HR 105), elevated lactate (2.8 mmol/L). Physical exam reveals LUQ tenderness without rebound or guarding. Initial FAST ultrasound negative for free fluid. No significant past medical history.
must_include_findings: splenic parenchyma for laceration, contusion, or hematoma

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of gastric malignancy and its extent/staging?
submission.pre_read_summary: 64M with poorly controlled Type 2 diabetes presenting with epigastric pain, early fullness, nausea, and 15-pound weight loss over several months. Physical exam shows mild epigastric tenderness. Previous imaging suggests delayed gastric emptying and focal narrowing near the distal stomach. Biopsy confirms malignant transformation involving the pyloric region. Family history includes mother with gastric adenocarcinoma.
must_include_findings: gastric wall thickening or mass lesion in the pyloric region

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in this neutropenic patient with febrile neutropenia?
submission.pre_read_summary: 54M with acute myeloid leukemia and history of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, currently undergoing induction chemotherapy. Patient developed profound neutropenia and presents with fever (38.9°C), chills, nonproductive cough, pleuritic chest pain, and mild shortness of breath. Broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy (cefepime and vancomycin) failed to improve symptoms. Blood cultures are negative, but serum galactomannan antigen testing is positive. Bronchoalveolar lavage grows Aspergillus fumigatus. Physical exam shows mild tenderness over right posterior thoracic area.
must_include_findings: nodular densities in the upper lobes

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of intracranial hemorrhage or other acute intracranial pathology in this 65M found unresponsive after suspected opioid overdose?
submission.pre_read_summary: 65M with severe opioid use disorder found unresponsive in his home after suspected overdose. Patient has history of cardiac arrest (2020) with resulting anterograde amnesia due to hippocampal injury. Currently intubated and in coma after 48 hours with severe respiratory acidosis (pH 7.11, pCO2 68, pO2 41). Neurologic exam shows no purposeful movement. EEG demonstrates diffuse slowing. On aspirin 81mg daily.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of acute pancreatitis?
submission.pre_read_summary: 23M with recurrent episodes of severe sharp upper abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. History of hyperzincemia diagnosed 6 months prior, currently taking zinc gluconate supplement 50 mg daily. Labs show elevated triglycerides (2000 mg/dL), amylase (2000 U/L), and lipase (1800 U/L). Physical exam reveals epigastric tenderness. Prior imaging ruled out gallstones or biliary obstruction. Family history of pancreatitis in father.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of deep vein thrombosis in the left lower extremity?
submission.pre_read_summary: 54-year-old female with progressive left calf pain and swelling for 3 days following a long car trip 2 weeks ago. Physical examination reveals erythematous, warm, tender left calf with pitting edema extending from ankle to mid-calf and 3 cm circumference difference from right calf. Risk factors include recent immobility, family history of DVT (father), and chronic prednisone use. Renal function is normal.
must_include_findings: any thrombus in other left lower extremity veins

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of acute intracranial pathology (intracerebral hemorrhage) causing the patient's unresponsiveness?
submission.pre_read_summary: 26M with myotonic dystrophy type 1 and exogenous androgen use (testosterone cypionate 200mg IM weekly) presents unresponsive at home after complaining of severe headache earlier in the day. Patient has secondary polycythemia (hemoglobin up to 19.2 g/dL) and renal tubular acidosis. Vitals: BP 150/90, HR 60. Physical exam shows unresponsive patient with fixed, dilated pupils, no ocular response, intubated with no spontaneous respirations. Apnea test shows no respiratory effort with PaCO2 rising to 60 mmHg.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of polyhydramnios and what are the potential underlying causes in this 28-year-old primigravida at 28 weeks gestation with a retained copper IUD and placenta previa?
submission.pre_read_summary: 28-year-old female at 28 weeks gestation presenting with increasing maternal abdominal distension and suspected polyhydramnios. Patient has a retained copper intrauterine device in situ and placenta previa. Physical exam shows fundal height greater than expected for gestational age. Previous ultrasound at 28 weeks gestation revealed excessive amniotic fluid with increased amniotic fluid index and normal Doppler studies. Family history includes paternal VACTERL association features (congenital vertebral anomalies). No maternal diabetes or fetal anomalies documented to date.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of structural brain pathology explaining the altered mental status and psychotic symptoms?
submission.pre_read_summary: 23M with known schizophrenia presenting with acute worsening of psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, paranoid ideation) over 2 weeks. Brought to ED for evaluation of altered mental status. Labs unremarkable.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of a molar pregnancy (hydatidiform mole) or other gestational trophoblastic disease causing vaginal bleeding in this pregnant patient?
submission.pre_read_summary: 27-year-old female with history of preterm birth at 32 weeks gestation presents with intermittent vaginal bleeding and pelvic pressure for 2 weeks, now worsening with increasing bleeding and lower abdominal pain. She has not received prenatal care for this pregnancy. Physical exam reveals a uterus larger than expected for gestational age. Laboratory evaluation shows markedly elevated β-hCG (250,000 mIU/mL, significantly above expected range for gestational age). Pelvic ultrasound demonstrates a snowstorm pattern without evidence of a fetus and bilateral enlarged multicystic ovaries. Family history is significant for maternal aunt with gestational trophoblastic disease.
must_include_findings: Absence of fetal pole on ultrasound
Uterus larger than expected for gestational age

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of acute ischemic stroke or hemorrhage in this patient presenting with sudden onset left-sided weakness and slurred speech?
submission.pre_read_summary: 71-year-old male with significant vascular risk factors (hypertension, type 2 diabetes, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation diagnosed 2020-01-15) presents to ED with sudden onset left-sided weakness and slurred speech for 2 hours. NIH Stroke Scale score is 12. Physical exam reveals left facial droop, left arm and leg weakness, and dysarthria. Patient is on warfarin 5mg daily. Noncontrast CT head performed to rule out hemorrhage shows no acute abnormalities.
must_include_findings: No acute infarct visible on noncontrast CT

submission.clinical_question: Is there a fracture of the left humerus?
submission.pre_read_summary: 33M with history of left humeral fracture (ORIF 2020-01-15) presenting after fall from ladder while repairing roof with immediate sharp pain in left upper arm. Physical exam shows significant swelling, bruising, and deformity over midportion of left humerus. Neurologic deficit noted: decreased sensation over dorsal aspect of left hand and thumb, unable to lift or extend left wrist or fingers. Radial and ulnar pulses present. X-ray of left upper extremity ordered to evaluate for fracture.
must_include_findings: displacement and alignment of humeral shaft
neurovascular status of left upper extremity

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of bladder endometriosis or other pelvic pathology causing cyclical hematuria?
submission.pre_read_summary: 30-year-old female with known endometriosis (ovary and bladder involvement) presenting with 6-month history of cyclical hematuria and dysuria that worsens during menses. Urinalysis confirms hematuria without infection. Cystoscopy reveals blue-tinged nodules on bladder wall consistent with bladder endometriosis. Pelvic ultrasound previously unremarkable. Patient also has polycystic ovary syndrome, primary infertility, and chronic pelvic pain. Currently on clomiphene citrate for ovulation induction.
must_include_findings: Bladder wall appearance for endometriosis nodules, thickening, or masses
Uterus and adnexa for ovarian endometriosis, cysts, or masses

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of recurrent or progressive invasive ductal carcinoma in the left breast?
submission.pre_read_summary: 52-year-old female with known invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast (ER+, PR+, HER2/neu negative) presents with a new palpable lump in the left breast discovered one month ago. Physical examination reveals a 2 cm firm, non-tender mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. Prior imaging shows a 2.1 cm irregular mass with spiculated margins. This mammography is ordered to evaluate the current breast mass for characterization, staging, and assessment of disease progression or recurrence.
must_include_findings: Size and dimensions of the left breast mass
Margins of the mass (spiculated, circumscribed, or indistinct)
Internal density and composition of the mass
Axillary lymph node assessment for metastatic disease

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of mediastinal lymphadenopathy or other pathology related to the neck mass?
submission.pre_read_summary: 16-year-old female with 6-week history of progressively enlarging painless left neck mass, associated B symptoms (night sweats, weight loss, fatigue), and generalized pruritus. Physical exam reveals firm, rubbery, non-tender left supraclavicular mass with generalized lymphadenopathy. Labs show anemia (Hgb 10.2), elevated ESR, and elevated ferritin. Chest X-ray demonstrates widened mediastinum. Lymph node biopsy is pending.

submission.clinical_question: Is the new right lower lobe consolidation on chest X-ray due to lung cancer recurrence/progression, pneumonia, or other etiology?
submission.pre_read_summary: 65M with history of Stage IIIB non-small cell lung cancer (6 months post-chemoradiation), COPD, and Type 2 diabetes. Presents with new onset cough and shortness of breath. Physical exam reveals decreased breath sounds in the right lower lung field. Labs show mild leukocytosis (WBC 12,000). Chest X-ray demonstrates a new right lower lobe consolidation.
must_include_findings: Assessment of lung volumes and pleural spaces

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of soft tissue injury, compartment syndrome, or vascular injury in the hand following trauma?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32M with history of right hand fasciotomy for compartment syndrome following crush injury. Current presentation involves left lower leg trauma from motorcycle accident. Imaging order is for ultrasound of upper extremity (hand) with indication of hand trauma. Patient has no current medications and is NKDA.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of a structural cause for elevated intracranial pressure in a 35-year-old obese female with headache, papilledema, and transient visual obscurations?
submission.pre_read_summary: 35-year-old female with obesity (BMI 35) presenting with 2-month history of daily headaches worse in the morning, transient visual obscurations, and pulsatile tinnitus. Physical exam reveals bilateral papilledema with intact visual acuity and fields. Lumbar puncture shows elevated opening pressure of 280 mmH2O. Previous MRI brain with and without contrast was normal. Clinical suspicion for idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is high given the classic presentation in an obese female of childbearing age with normal neuroimaging.
must_include_findings: No mass lesion or space-occupying lesion

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of recurrent aortic dissection in this patient with prior Type A aortic dissection presenting with acute tearing chest/back pain?
submission.pre_read_summary: 52-year-old male with history of Type A aortic dissection (diagnosed 2020-01-15) and hypertension presents with sudden-onset severe upper back pain radiating between scapulae. Pain described as tearing and worse than previous episodes. Patient is diaphoretic with BP 188/92, HR 106/min. Prior encounters (2020-01-15) showed widened mediastinum on CXR and confirmed Type A aortic dissection. Current ECG shows nonspecific ST-T changes. Patient is a current smoker (30 pack-years) with family history of aortic aneurysm and sudden cardiac death.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of carotid artery stenosis as a cause of the patient's TIA symptoms?
submission.pre_read_summary: 67-year-old male with history of cerebrovascular disease, poorly controlled hypertension, peripheral artery disease, and coronary artery disease presents with sudden onset of right arm weakness and difficulty speaking that resolved within one hour (TIA). Physical exam reveals carotid bruit. Previous imaging shows 75% stenosis of left internal carotid artery. Patient is on antiplatelet therapy (aspirin) and antihypertensive medications.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of a renal malignancy causing gross hematuria?
submission.pre_read_summary: 57-year-old female with history of gastric surgery (partial gastrectomy with Billroth II reconstruction, revision distal gastrectomy) presents with visible hematuria over 3 days, dull left-sided flank pain, and 10-kg weight loss over 2 months. Physical exam shows left costovertebral angle tenderness. Prior renal ultrasound reveals a heterogenous mass in the left kidney.
must_include_findings: Heterogenous mass in the left kidney

differential.diagnosis: Transitional cell carcinoma of renal pelvis

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of intra-abdominal infection, bowel ischemia, or other acute abdominal pathology in a 68M with pancreatic adenocarcinoma presenting with sepsis (fever, hypotension, tachycardia) and gram-negative bacteremia?
submission.pre_read_summary: 68M with known mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma and chronic DIC presents to ICU with acute worsening abdominal pain, fever (39.4°C), rigors, confusion, and signs of sepsis (hypotension 84/52, tachycardia 128/min, tachypnea 28/min). Blood cultures grow gram-negative rods. Labs show leukocytosis with left shift, elevated lactate, worsening creatinine, and climbing liver enzymes. Physical exam reveals diffusely tender abdomen with hypoactive bowel sounds. Prior CT (2023) showed pancreatic mass with biliary dilation. Current imaging concern is for intra-abdominal infection, bowel ischemia, or complications of pancreatic malignancy.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of structural brain abnormalities (cortical tubers, subependymal nodules) consistent with tuberous sclerosis complex that could be contributing to refractory epilepsy?
submission.pre_read_summary: 3M with refractory epilepsy since infancy (seizures began at 6 months), global developmental delay, and history of nephrolithiasis. Physical exam reveals hypopigmented macules on back (ash-leaf spots). Previous imaging showed cardiac rhabdomyoma. MRI of head ordered to evaluate for cortical tubers and subependymal nodules consistent with tuberous sclerosis complex.

differential.diagnosis: Other causes of refractory epilepsy in children

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of worsening pulmonary hypertension or other structural abnormalities contributing to respiratory distress in this infant with VACTERL association, PPHN, and coarctation of the aorta?
submission.pre_read_summary: Male infant with VACTERL association, status post TEF repair and PUV ablation, presenting with respiratory distress and poor feeding for 2 days after discharge at 2 days of life. Known history of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn and coarctation of the aorta. Current vitals: RR 60, HR 160, O2 sat 92% on room air. Physical exam shows absent femoral pulses, grade 3/6 systolic murmur, and hepatomegaly. Chest X-ray demonstrates cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings. Currently on Alprostadil for PPHN management.
must_include_findings: pulmonary artery diameter and flow velocities
evidence of pulmonary hypertension on Doppler assessment

differential.diagnosis: Worsening persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
Congestive heart failure secondary to coarctation of the aorta

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of intra-abdominal complications of Crohn disease such as abscess, fistula, or bowel obstruction in this patient with bloody diarrhea?
submission.pre_read_summary: 27-year-old female with known Crohn disease presenting with 6-month history of intermittent bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss. Physical exam shows mild left lower quadrant tenderness. Labs demonstrate anemia (Hb 10.2 g/dL), elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 45 mm/hr, CRP 25 mg/L), and hypoalbuminemia (3.2 g/dL). Stool cultures and C. diff toxin negative. Colonoscopy reveals continuous mucosal inflammation and ulceration from rectum to splenic flexure with pseudopolyps. Pathology shows chronic inflammation limited to mucosa and submucosa. Abdomen/pelvis imaging ordered to evaluate for intra-abdominal complications.

submission.clinical_question: Is the right breast mass benign or malignant?
submission.pre_read_summary: 42-year-old female presents with a palpable, non-tender, smooth, mobile mass in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast discovered one month ago. She has a history of fibrocystic breast changes and two prior benign breast biopsies. No family history of breast cancer. Last mammogram 18 months ago was normal. Physical exam shows a smooth, mobile mass with no axillary lymphadenopathy. Ultrasound reveals a simple cyst measuring 2 cm in diameter that completely resolves on post-aspiration. Fine-needle aspiration yields straw-colored, non-bloody fluid.
must_include_findings: Simple cyst measuring 2 cm in diameter
Cyst completely resolves on post-aspiration ultrasound
No solid components or suspicious features

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of progression of iron deposition arthropathy or other pathology in the hands?
submission.pre_read_summary: 41M with known hereditary hemochromatosis and iron deposition arthropathy, presenting with progressive bilateral hand joint pain and stiffness for 6 months, particularly affecting second and third MCP joints. Previously diagnosed with porphyria cutanea tarda (2020) with skin fragility and blistering on dorsal hands. Current labs show elevated iron studies (ferritin 600 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 72%). Physical exam reveals swelling and tenderness over second and third MCP joints and wrists. Prior radiographs showed chondrocalcinosis and joint space narrowing.
must_include_findings: Joint space narrowing at MCP joints

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of ectopic pregnancy or pregnancy-related complication causing vaginal bleeding in this 30-year-old female at approximately 8 weeks gestation?
submission.pre_read_summary: 30-year-old female at approximately 8 weeks gestation presenting with 6-hour history of vaginal bleeding and lower abdominal cramping. Patient has history of Hashimoto's thyroiditis and inadequately controlled hypothyroidism during pregnancy. Quantitative beta-hCG is 12,000 mIU/mL consistent with pregnancy. Physical exam shows soft, enlarged uterus consistent with 8-week gestation. Bedside ultrasound reveals gestational sac in lower uterine segment with no fetal heart activity.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of cervical shortening or funneling in a 30-year-old female at term gestation presenting with regular uterine contractions and lower back pain, to assess risk of preterm delivery?
submission.pre_read_summary: 30-year-old female at term gestation presenting to ED with 4-hour history of regular uterine contractions and lower back pain. History of gestational hypertension (mild, without proteinuria, controlled with diet). Physical exam shows irritable uterus with palpable contractions every 5 minutes, fetal heart tones 140-142 bpm, closed cervical os without bleeding or fluid leakage. Fetal fibronectin test positive. Transvaginal ultrasound ordered to assess cervical length and evaluate for cervical shortening/funneling in the context of uterine contractions.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pneumonia in this patient with fever, productive cough, and shortness of breath?
submission.pre_read_summary: 64-year-old male with mechanical aortic valve replacement, osteoporosis, and recent femoral fracture admission. On hospital day 5, developed fever (38.5°C), productive cough, and shortness of breath. Physical exam reveals crackles in right lower lung field. Sputum culture grows Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Chest x-ray shows new right lower lobe infiltrate.
must_include_findings: Crackles in right lower lung field

submission.clinical_question: What is the cause of progressive dyspnea, fever, and bilateral interstitial infiltrates in this HIV-positive patient with CD4 count of 50?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32M with HIV infection (AIDS) and CD4 count of 50/mm3, non-adherent to ART for 6 months, presenting with 3-week history of progressive dyspnea, nonproductive cough, fever, night sweats, and 10-pound weight loss. Physical exam reveals tachypnea (RR 28), hypoxemia (O2 sat 88%), and bilateral diffuse crackles. Chest X-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates. History of prior Pneumocystis pneumonia (diagnosed 2020-01-15).

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of nephrolithiasis causing the patient's right flank pain?
submission.pre_read_summary: 46M with history of recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis presenting with 2-day history of severe right flank pain radiating to groin, nausea, and vomiting. Physical exam shows right costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis demonstrates hematuria without signs of infection. Prior non-contrast CT showed 5 mm calculus in right ureter.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of fetal growth restriction or abnormal fetal growth in this pregnant patient with preeclampsia?
submission.pre_read_summary: 30-year-old pregnant female with mild preeclampsia without severe features, presenting with persistent headache and upper abdominal discomfort. History of gestational hypertension in prior pregnancy. Current BP 150/98 mm Hg with 2+ proteinuria. Previous ultrasound (2020-01-15) showed appropriate fetal size for gestational age with normal amniotic fluid. Doppler velocimetry showed high-resistance blood flow with reduced diastolic flow velocity in uterine arteries. Current imaging ordered to assess fetal growth parameters.
must_include_findings: Fetal biometry measurements (BPD, HC, AC, FL)

differential.diagnosis: Normal fetal growth - appropriate for gestational age

submission.clinical_question: What is the cause of new-onset cough and shortness of breath in a 64M with known lisinopril allergy and chronic DIC secondary to malignancy?
submission.pre_read_summary: 64M with history of hypertension, CAD, laryngeal SCC, and chronic DIC secondary to malignancy. Presents with new-onset cough and shortness of breath starting 2 weeks after initiating lisinopril therapy. Patient has known lisinopril allergy (angioedema/cough). Physical exam reveals bilateral crackles at lung bases. Vitals: BP 130/85, HR 78, O2 sat 94% on room air. Labs: normal WBC, Hgb, platelets, Cr; BNP 80 pg/mL (normal). Chest X-ray shows no infiltrates but mild pulmonary congestion. Differential includes ACE-inhibitor induced cough, drug-induced pulmonary edema, pulmonary embolism (given chronic DIC), and heart failure exacerbation.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of intrauterine fetal death given decreased fetal movement?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32-year-old female at approximately 32 weeks gestation (abdomen appropriately sized for gestational age) presenting to ED with complaint of decreased fetal movement since the previous evening. Patient has history of placenta previa (diagnosed 2020-01-15) and severe fetal anemia due to fetomaternal hemorrhage (diagnosed 2020-06-15). On physical exam, no fetal heart tones detected on auscultation. Bedside ultrasound performed to evaluate fetal viability.
must_include_findings: Abdomen appropriately sized for gestational age
No vaginal bleeding or fluid leakage reported

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of plantar fasciitis, stress fracture, or other pathology causing heel pain in this 45-year-old female runner?
submission.pre_read_summary: 45-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic hypertension, obesity, and polycystic ovary syndrome presents with a 2-month history of heel pain that is severe with first steps in the morning or after rest, exacerbated by recent increase in running mileage. She is an avid runner preparing for a marathon. Physical exam demonstrates tenderness at the anteromedial aspect of the calcaneus with pain on passive dorsiflexion of toes, but no swelling or erythema. Plain radiographs of the foot show no fractures or calcifications.
must_include_findings: No fractures or calcifications on plain radiographs
Assessment of plantar fascia for thickening or calcification
Evaluation of calcaneus for stress reaction or fracture
Assessment of surrounding soft tissues for inflammation or abnormality

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of osteomyelitis or other complications from the right foot nail puncture wound?
submission.pre_read_summary: 25M with right foot puncture wound from nail 5 days ago, presenting with 2-day history of increasing pain, redness, and swelling on the sole of his right foot. Physical exam shows 1 cm puncture wound with surrounding erythema, warmth, and tenderness on the plantar surface of the right foot. Labs show leukocytosis (WBC 12,000/uL) and elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 45 mm/hr, CRP 25 mg/L). Prior imaging shows no fractures but evidence of periosteal reaction along the proximal phalanx of the second toe.
must_include_findings: 1 cm puncture wound with surrounding erythema, warmth, and tenderness on plantar surface of right foot
Periosteal reaction along proximal phalanx of second toe

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of active pulmonary tuberculosis or complications such as cavitation, abscess, or other pulmonary pathology in this patient with known TB diagnosis?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32-year-old Filipino male with known tuberculosis diagnosis (diagnosed 2020-01-15) presenting with 3-week history of productive cough, night sweats, 5kg weight loss, and fever (38.6°C). Physical exam reveals decreased breath sounds in right upper lobe. Prior imaging (2020-01-15) showed right apical infiltrate. Current labs show leukocytosis (12,000 cells/µL) with left shift. First sputum AFB stain was negative. Patient recently immigrated from a country with high TB prevalence and has not received vaccinations or medical care since arrival.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage or ischemic stroke in this patient with atrial fibrillation presenting with acute right-sided hemiparesis?
submission.pre_read_summary: 69M with known valvular atrial fibrillation and history of multiple thromboembolic events (DVT, mesenteric ischemia, arterial embolism) presents with acute-onset right arm and face weakness, facial droop, and inability to grip objects. Patient is alert and oriented with intact language. Non-contrast head CT ordered to evaluate for acute stroke (ischemic vs hemorrhagic).
must_include_findings: presence or absence of acute intracranial hemorrhage
presence or absence of acute ischemic changes

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of malignancy or progression of the known pulmonary nodule?
submission.pre_read_summary: 67-year-old male with 40-pack-year smoking history, COPD, and peripheral arterial disease. Known solitary pulmonary nodule (1.2 cm, spiculated margins in right upper lobe) identified on chest X-ray in January 2023, confirmed on CT without additional abnormalities. Patient presents to Neurology with increasing difficulty climbing stairs and rising from chair over 3 months, dry mouth, and intermittent double vision. Current chest X-ray reveals a right hilar mass. Active problem list includes "Solitary pulmonary nodule with high suspicion for malignancy" diagnosed 2023-01-15.
must_include_findings: Comparison to prior imaging showing 1.2 cm nodule in right upper lobe with spiculated margins
Assessment of nodule size, margins, and any interval change

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of structural or hormonal causes of secondary amenorrhea in this 17-year-old female with signs of an eating disorder?
submission.pre_read_summary: 17-year-old female with secondary amenorrhea for 8 months, BMI 16 kg/m², signs of eating disorder (excessive exercise, food restriction, lanugo hair, bradycardia, hypotension). Noncompliant with insulin for Type 1 Diabetes. Thyroid and prolactin levels normal. Pelvic ultrasound shows thin endometrium and small ovaries without cysts.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of significant mitral valve pathology contributing to the patient's symptoms of progressive dyspnea on exertion and palpitations?
submission.pre_read_summary: 37-year-old female presenting with 6-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion and palpitations. Physical examination reveals a high-pitched mid-systolic click followed by a late systolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla, classic for mitral valve prolapse. Family history is significant for maternal mitral valve prolapse and paternal aunt with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension. Previous transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated mitral valve leaflets with excessive motion during systole, significant mitral regurgitation, and left atrial enlargement. ECG shows atrial fibrillation with ventricular rate of 92 bpm. Patient is on ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone and multivitamin.
must_include_findings: Presence of intracardiac thrombus or vegetation

differential.diagnosis: Mitral valve prolapse with mitral regurgitation

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of active lower GI bleeding or vascular abnormalities in this patient with recurrent rectal bleeding?
submission.pre_read_summary: 72M with history of mechanical mitral valve, severe aortic stenosis, and gastrointestinal angiodysplasia presents with recurrent episodes of painless bright red blood per rectum over the past week. He is on warfarin (INR goal 2.5-3.5) and aspirin. Labs show hemoglobin of 9.3 g/dL (baseline 12.6), consistent with iron deficiency anemia. Prior nuclear medicine scan suggested bleeding from the cecum, and colonoscopy during active bleeding demonstrated small, flat, cherry-red lesions with ectatic vessels in the cecum consistent with angiodysplasia. Current abdominal CT angiography is unremarkable. Colonoscopy repeated shows no active source of bleeding.
must_include_findings: No evidence of active bleeding or vascular malformations
No evidence of diverticulosis, diverticulitis, or other vascular abnormalities
No evidence of mass or tumor

submission.clinical_question: Is the left breast mass malignant or benign?
submission.pre_read_summary: 29-year-old female presenting with a firm, non-tender 2.4-cm mass in the left breast upper outer quadrant detected during self-examination. Strong family history of breast cancer (sister diagnosed with bilateral breast cancer at age 35, mother at age 45, maternal grandmother died from ovarian cancer in late 40s). History of childhood Wilms tumor with abdominopelvic radiation therapy at age 6 and left nephrectomy. Also has Crohn disease on adalimumab therapy. Mammography reveals a suspicious irregular lesion. Core needle biopsy is pending.
must_include_findings: 2.4-cm mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast
no overlying skin changes or nipple retraction on physical exam

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of intracranial pathology (e.g., hemorrhage, mass, infarction) explaining the patient's altered mental status?
submission.pre_read_summary: 62-year-old female with metastatic breast cancer with osseous metastases, chronic kidney disease stage 4, and type 2 diabetes presents with acute confusion, lethargy, poor appetite, and worsening constipation over the past week. Physical exam reveals dry mucous membranes and mild lower extremity weakness. Laboratory studies demonstrate severe hypercalcemia (serum calcium 13.4 mg/dL) with suppressed PTH, consistent with malignancy-associated hypercalcemia. ECG shows shortened QT interval. Patient was admitted and received IV fluids and pamidronate with improvement in mental status over 24 hours. Non-contrast head CT performed to evaluate for intracranial causes of altered mental status.

differential.diagnosis: Metastatic breast cancer with osseous metastases

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of aortic dissection or esophageal rupture?
submission.pre_read_summary: 45-year-old male with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and primary hyperparathyroidism presents with sudden severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back following vomiting after heavy meal and alcohol consumption. Physical exam reveals subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and Hamman's sign (crunching sound synchronous with heartbeat). Chest X-ray shows mediastinal widening and small left pleural effusion. Vitals: BP 150/90, HR 110, RR 22. Leukocytosis (WBC 18,000). History of GERD and recurrent nephrolithiasis.

submission.clinical_question: Is there a renal mass in the left kidney and what are its characteristics?
submission.pre_read_summary: 4-year-old female presenting with 2-month history of gradually increasing abdominal swelling and hematuria. Physical exam reveals a firm, non-tender left flank mass. Vitals show elevated blood pressure (128/82). Labs show mild anemia (Hgb 11.2) with otherwise normal CBC and renal function. Urinalysis shows RBCs. Initial ultrasound shows a large, solid mass arising from the left kidney.
must_include_findings: Size and characteristics of the left renal mass
Any hydronephrosis or involvement of surrounding structures

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pneumonia or other acute pulmonary pathology in this patient with COPD exacerbation?
submission.pre_read_summary: 67-year-old male with moderate to severe COPD and 40-pack-year smoking history presents to ED with 3-day history of increased shortness of breath, productive cough with greenish sputum, and low-grade fever. Vitals show tachycardia (HR 102), tachypnea (RR 22), and hypoxia (O2 sat 89% on room air). Physical exam reveals diffuse wheezes and prolonged expiration. ABG shows respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia (pH 7.36, PaCO2 50, PaO2 60). Previous outpatient visit 3 months ago showed similar ABG findings. Chest radiography shows no consolidation but hyperinflated lung fields consistent with COPD.
must_include_findings: Hyperinflated lung fields consistent with COPD

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pulmonary embolism or other acute pulmonary pathology in this patient with progressive shortness of breath?
submission.pre_read_summary: 34-year-old male with 1-year history of progressive shortness of breath, active smoker (22.5 pack-year history), known emphysema on prior imaging, and thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger disease). Physical exam reveals diminished breath sounds bilaterally with hyperresonant percussion at lung bases. Family history of lung disease in brother. Also has history of headaches, palpitations, and elevated blood pressure with bilateral renal cysts suggestive of ADPKD.
must_include_findings: pulmonary vasculature for evidence of pulmonary embolism
lung parenchyma for masses, consolidation, or interstitial disease
pleural spaces for pneumothorax or effusion

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE)?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32F with recent high-altitude exposure (12,000 feet over 2 days) presenting with progressive shortness of breath and dry cough. Hypoxemic (O2 sat 86% on room air, PaO2 55 mmHg) with tachypnea (RR 26/min) and bilateral crackles on exam. Family history of high-altitude pulmonary edema susceptibility (maternal aunt). Chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral alveolar infiltrates.
must_include_findings: Bilateral alveolar infiltrates on chest X-ray
Hypoxemia (PaO2 55 mmHg, O2 sat 86% on room air)

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of osteoarthritis or other pathology in the right knee causing mechanical pain in this obese patient?
submission.pre_read_summary: 52F with obesity (BMI 34), Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and acanthosis nigricans presents with progressive right knee pain over 3 months. Pain is worse with activity and improves with rest (mechanical pattern). Physical exam shows tenderness over medial tibial condyle with pain on resisted flexion. No erythema or warmth. Previous x-ray shows mild joint space narrowing without fracture.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of ventriculoperitoneal shunt malfunction or obstruction given the patient's symptoms of irritability, vomiting, and excessive sleepiness?
submission.pre_read_summary: 3-year-old male with Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome and congenital hydrocephalus dependent on ventriculoperitoneal shunt. Presents with 2-day history of irritability, high-pitched crying, forceful vomiting, and excessive sleepiness. Physical exam reveals lethargy, full/tense anterior fontanelle, and bilateral papilledema. Recent head ultrasound demonstrates dilated lateral ventricles. Patient has history of multiple prior neurosurgical encounters for shunt-related symptoms. Current presentation is highly concerning for shunt malfunction with signs of increased intracranial pressure.
must_include_findings: Evidence of shunt obstruction or malfunction

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of right-sided renal pathology (pyelonephritis, obstruction, or other complications) causing the patient's left flank pain and fever, considering the history of left nephrectomy and recurrent nephrolithiasis?
submission.pre_read_summary: 52-year-old female with history of left nephrectomy, recurrent nephrolithiasis, and recurrent UTIs. Presents with left flank pain, fever, and hematuria. Urinalysis shows infection (leukocytes, blood, struvite crystals). Imaging reveals large staghorn calculus in left renal pelvis. Patient has contrast dye allergy (anaphylaxis).
must_include_findings: Evaluation of right kidney for pyelonephritis, obstruction, or other pathology
Evaluation for abscess or other complications

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of infective endocarditis in this immunocompromised patient with fever, new murmur, and recent urinary catheterization?
submission.pre_read_summary: 71-year-old male with chronic lymphocytic leukemia, Paget disease, and benign prostatic hyperpasia presents with fever (38.9°C), chills, dysuria, and a new grade 2/6 systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border not previously documented. Recent hospitalization 2 weeks ago for acute urinary retention with Foley catheter placement. Laboratory findings include leukocytosis (WBC 14,000/uL) and urinalysis consistent with UTI (pyuria, positive leukocyte esterase and nitrite). Blood cultures pending. Echocardiogram ordered to evaluate for infective endocarditis given the combination of fever, new cardiac murmur, and recent invasive instrumentation.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of a lung mass and/or metastatic disease in this patient with known follicular lymphoma presenting with fatigue and weight loss?
submission.pre_read_summary: 64F with known follicular lymphoma (diagnosed 2020-07-15) and 40-pack-year smoking history presents with 3-month history of progressive fatigue and 10-pound unintentional weight loss. Physical exam reveals cachexia and decreased breath sounds in right lower lobe. Chest X-ray demonstrates a 4 cm mass in the right lower lobe. Pathology confirms non-small cell lung cancer. CT-guided biopsy of the mass performed.
must_include_findings: 4 cm mass in right lower lobe

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, or cholangitis in this post-cholecystectomy patient presenting with RUQ pain and fever?
submission.pre_read_summary: 28-year-old female with history of laparoscopic cholecystectomy at age 26 presents with 2-day history of intermittent right upper quadrant pain radiating to back, fever (38.9°C), chills, and jaundice. Physical exam reveals RUQ tenderness with positive Murphy's sign. Laboratory results show leukocytosis (WBC 15,000/mm³), elevated total bilirubin (3.2 mg/dL with direct 2.5 mg/dL), and elevated alkaline phosphatase (190 U/L). Previous ultrasound showed multiple gallstones. Current imaging order is RUQ ultrasound to evaluate for recurrent biliary pathology.

submission.clinical_question: Is the fetus in breech presentation and are there any other relevant findings such as placental location, amniotic fluid volume, or fetal anomalies?
submission.pre_read_summary: 34-year-old African American female at routine prenatal visit. History of uterine leiomyomas, gestational hypertension, classical cesarean section, and prior breech presentation at 36 weeks gestation. Current pregnancy with suspected breech position on palpation. Patient reports occasional shortness of breath. Physical exam shows fundal height consistent with gestational age with suspected breech fetal position.
must_include_findings: placental location and relationship to internal cervical os

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of aortic dissection?
submission.pre_read_summary: 55M with known bicuspid aortic valve and strong family history of aortic pathology (father with bicuspid aortic valve diagnosed at age 50, paternal uncle died of ruptured ascending aortic aneurysm at age 64). Presents with sudden, severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back while lifting heavy boxes. Significant blood pressure differential between arms (95/50 mmHg right vs 75/40 mmHg left). Physical exam shows diminished femoral pulses and muffled heart sounds. Chest x-ray demonstrates widened mediastinum. ECG shows nonspecific ST and T wave changes. This clinical picture is highly concerning for aortic dissection.

differential.diagnosis: Aortic dissection (Type A or Type B)

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of an intracranial lesion (e.g., opportunistic infection, neoplasm, or vascular event) explaining this patient's progressive confusion, headache, and focal neurologic deficits?
submission.pre_read_summary: 44-year-old female with HIV/AIDS (CD4 count 70 cells/mm³) and history of CMV esophagitis presents with progressive confusion and headache over the past week, now nonverbal and lethargic. Neurologic exam reveals disorientation and mild right-sided weakness. Patient has history of opioid use disorder in remission. Recent ED visit (July 2020) noted retinal whitening and hemorrhage in left eye, suggestive of CMV retinitis. CT head ordered to evaluate for intracranial pathology.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pelvic fracture or hip dislocation following motor vehicle collision trauma?
submission.pre_read_summary: 22M involved in head-on motor vehicle collision with knees hitting dashboard, presenting to ED with severe right hip pain and inability to move right leg. Physical exam shows right leg shortened and internally rotated with inability to dorsiflex right foot. Pelvic X-ray performed to rule out fracture.
must_include_findings: Posterior dislocation of the right hip
Any associated pelvic or femoral fractures

submission.clinical_question: Is the 6 mm non-calcified pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe malignant or benign, and what is the appropriate management strategy?
submission.pre_read_summary: 45-year-old male with COPD and 30-pack-year smoking history, family history of lung cancer (paternal uncle). Presents for follow-up evaluation of a 6 mm non-calcified nodule in the right lower lobe incidentally discovered on screening low-dose CT chest. Patient is asymptomatic. Active problems include COPD and tobacco use disorder. Previous screening in January 2020 was for lung cancer risk assessment.
must_include_findings: 6 mm non-calcified nodule in right lower lobe
comparison with prior imaging if available

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of heart failure or cardiac decompensation in this infant with known hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and repaired Tetralogy of Fallot?
submission.pre_read_summary: Infant with complex congenital cardiac history including repaired Tetralogy of Fallot and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Also has Pompe disease (suggested by elevated creatine kinase, muscle biopsy showing glycogen vacuoles, and on alglucosidase alfa enzyme replacement). Presents with feeding difficulties, poor weight gain, and progressive hypotonia. Physical exam reveals gallop rhythm. Recent imaging demonstrates marked cardiomegaly. Current chest X-ray ordered for cardiac evaluation to assess for heart failure, pulmonary edema, or other cardiac complications.

differential.diagnosis: Congestive heart failure secondary to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Residual cardiac complications from Tetralogy of Fallot repair

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of structural brain pathology or hydrocephalus explaining the patient's altered mental status and worsening psychiatric symptoms?
submission.pre_read_summary: 25M with known treatment-resistant schizophrenia on clozapine 300mg daily presents to ED with worsening psychiatric symptoms over 6 months including social withdrawal, bizarre behavior, and delusions of thought control. Patient has history of oculogyric crisis after haloperidol exposure. Urine toxicology negative. Non-contrast head CT shows enlargement of lateral cerebral ventricles. Neurological exam unremarkable.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pulmonary hypertension and right heart strain secondary to obstructive sleep apnea?
submission.pre_read_summary: 53M with obesity (BMI 35), hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia presenting with daytime sleepiness and morning headaches. Physical exam reveals enlarged neck circumference and pitting edema. ABG demonstrates respiratory acidosis (PaCO2 55 mmHg, PaO2 68 mmHg) with compensatory metabolic alkalosis. CBC shows polycythemia (Hgb 18.5 g/dL, Hct 55%). Prior echocardiogram shows right ventricular hypertrophy. Chest ultrasound ordered to evaluate for pulmonary hypertension and right heart strain secondary to suspected obstructive sleep apnea.

differential.diagnosis: Obstructive sleep apnea with pulmonary hypertension

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of traumatic pulmonary injury (pulmonary contusion, pneumothorax, hemothorax) in this patient following high-speed motor vehicle collision?
submission.pre_read_summary: 22M with high-speed motor vehicle collision presenting with severe pelvic pain, difficulty breathing, and hypoxemia (O2 sat 89%, PaO2 60 mmHg). Physical exam reveals unstable pelvis, bilateral lung crackles, and petechial rash. Chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral diffuse infiltrates.
must_include_findings: hypoxemia with O2 sat 89% and PaO2 60 mmHg

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of renal artery stenosis in this 33-year-old female with newly diagnosed hypertension, headaches, fatigue, and a right-sided abdominal bruit?
submission.pre_read_summary: 33-year-old female presenting with newly diagnosed hypertension (168/100 mmHg), headaches, and fatigue over several weeks. Physical exam reveals a right-sided abdominal bruit audible near the umbilicus. Family history significant for hypertension (mother diagnosed age 32), renal artery stenosis (paternal uncle), and ischemic stroke (father at age 48). Laboratory tests including renal function and electrolytes are normal. CT angiography of abdomen ordered to evaluate for renal artery stenosis.
must_include_findings: Evidence of renal artery stenosis (narrowing, occlusion)

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of thymoma in this patient with myasthenia gravis and anterior mediastinal mass?
submission.pre_read_summary: 28-year-old female with myasthenia gravis diagnosed in January 2020, presenting with recurrent intermittent double vision, bilateral ptosis, dysphagia, and slurred speech. Symptoms fluctuate and worsen with fatigue, improving with rest. Patient has been on pyridostigmine 60mg TID since diagnosis. CT chest reveals an anterior mediastinal mass. Evaluation for thymoma given the association between myasthenia gravis and thymic tumors.
must_include_findings: anterior mediastinal mass location and size

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of orbital cellulitis with abscess formation or complications in a 7-year-old male with fever, left periorbital swelling, proptosis, and pain on eye movement?
submission.pre_read_summary: 7-year-old male with chronic rhinosinusitis presenting with 3-day history of fever (38.9°C), worsening left eye pain, and periorbital swelling. Physical exam reveals erythematous and edematous left eyelids, proptosis, pain with extraocular movements, and decreased visual acuity. Labs show leukocytosis (WBC 15,000/mm³) with neutrophilia (80%) and elevated ESR (45 mm/hr). History of recurrent upper respiratory infections and prior orbital cellulitis (2020-07-15). CT of orbits ordered to evaluate extent of orbital infection and rule out complications.
must_include_findings: soft tissue mass in left orbit

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of structural brain pathology (e.g., tumor, stroke, normal pressure hydrocephalus, atypical parkinsonism) that could explain the patient's progressive tremor and movement disorder symptoms?
submission.pre_read_summary: 68M with known Parkinson Disease Psychosis presenting with progressive bradykinesia, rigidity, shuffling gait, and resting tremor over the past year. Currently on carbidopa-levodopa, ropinirole, rasagiline, and sertraline. Physical exam reveals cogwheel rigidity, masked facies, and positive pull test. Family history significant for Parkinson disease (father, onset age 72) and essential tremor (sister). MRI of brain ordered to evaluate for structural etiology of movement disorder.
must_include_findings: No evidence of acute or chronic infarction
No evidence of normal pressure hydrocephalus

differential.diagnosis: Atypical parkinsonism (multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy)

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of myocardial ischemia in this patient with recurrent exertional chest pain and history of acute MI?
submission.pre_read_summary: 58M with history of acute MI (6 months prior), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, presenting with recurrent exertional chest pain radiating to left arm. Undergoing nuclear chest imaging (SPECT MPI) for chest pain evaluation. Physical exam unremarkable, ECG no acute changes.
must_include_findings: reversible defect in anterior wall on stress images

differential.diagnosis: Coronary artery disease with myocardial ischemia

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of severe aortic stenosis causing exertional dyspnea and decreased exercise tolerance?
submission.pre_read_summary: 78-year-old female with history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and atrial fibrillation presents with 6-month history of progressive exertional dyspnea, decreased exercise tolerance, occasional chest tightness, and dizziness when climbing stairs. Physical examination reveals a harsh, crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur at the right second intercostal space radiating to carotids (classic for aortic stenosis). Prior echocardiography demonstrates calcified aortic valve with restricted leaflet motion and aortic valve area of 0.9 cm² (severe). ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy. No JVD, lungs clear to auscultation.

differential.diagnosis: Atrial fibrillation with reduced cardiac output

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of lymphoma given the cervical lymphadenopathy, B symptoms, and mediastinal widening?
submission.pre_read_summary: 27-year-old female presenting with 2-month history of painless cervical lymphadenopathy, B symptoms (intermittent fevers, night sweats, 5 kg weight loss), and mediastinal widening on chest X-ray. Physical exam reveals bilateral rubbery, non-tender cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes. Laboratory studies show elevated ESR (50 mm/hr) with otherwise normal CBC. Family history significant for paternal cousin with Hodgkin lymphoma (diagnosed age 26).

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of lung cancer or suspicious pulmonary nodules/masses in this high-risk smoker?
submission.pre_read_summary: 58M with tobacco use disorder and COPD, presenting for lung cancer screening given smoking history and family history of lung cancer (father deceased at age 62). Recent chest X-ray was unremarkable. Patient is asymptomatic with no acute complaints.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of infantile spasms and underlying structural brain abnormalities, particularly Tuberous Sclerosis Complex?
submission.pre_read_summary: 0M with new-onset episodes of staring spells and spasms occurring multiple times daily for 2 months. Known history of cardiac rhabdomyoma, global developmental delay, and prenatal alcohol exposure. Currently on vigabatrin 50 mg/kg/day for suspected infantile spasms. Previous imaging (2020-05-15) shows posterior fossa cystic malformation with hydrocephalus. Current MRI findings include subependymal nodules and cortical tubers, consistent with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. EEG shows hypsarrhythmia. Physical exam reveals hypopigmented macules and raised flesh-colored plaque. Family history of seizures in maternal uncle.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of progression of metastatic breast cancer to the liver or other cause of worsening right upper quadrant pain?
submission.pre_read_summary: 57-year-old female with known metastatic breast carcinoma to liver and adrenal glands presents with progressive right upper quadrant pain and 10 kg weight loss over 2 months. Physical exam shows mild RUQ tenderness without jaundice or ascites. Labs demonstrate mild elevation in alkaline phosphatase with normal bilirubin. Previous imaging (abdominal ultrasound) shows multiple hypoechoic liver lesions. Current CT abdomen is being performed to evaluate the cause of worsening RUQ pain and assess for progression of liver metastases.

differential.diagnosis: Progression of metastatic breast cancer to liver

submission.clinical_question: What is the etiology of progressive abdominal distension, early satiety, and weight loss in a 58-year-old female with known pancreatic carcinoma, characterized by ascites, pelvic masses, and omental thickening on CT?
submission.pre_read_summary: 58-year-old female with history of pancreatic carcinoma (diagnosed 2024), chronic pancreatitis, and Type 2 diabetes presents with 3-month history of progressive abdominal fullness, early satiety, and 6 kg unintentional weight loss. Physical exam reveals abdominal distension with shifting dullness and fluid wave, and bilateral adnexal fullness. CT abdomen/pelvis demonstrates large volume ascites, multiple solid pelvic masses, and diffuse omental thickening. Family history notable for father's pancreatic adenocarcinoma, maternal grandmother's ovarian cancer, and sister's breast cancer.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pneumonia or other acute pulmonary pathology in this patient with COPD exacerbation?
submission.pre_read_summary: 68M with GOLD Stage IV COPD on home oxygen presents with 3-day history of increased shortness of breath, productive cough with greenish sputum, and wheezing. Fever 38.5°C, tachypneic (RR 28), tachycardic (HR 110), O2 sat 88% on room air. ABG shows respiratory acidosis (pH 7.32, PaCO2 50, PaO2 60). Previous encounters in Jan and April 2020 for similar complaints. CXR shows hyperinflated lungs with no consolidation.

submission.clinical_question: What is the cause of vaginal bleeding at 12 weeks gestation, and does the pelvic ultrasound demonstrate a molar pregnancy, threatened miscarriage, or other pathology?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32-year-old female at 12 weeks gestation presenting with acute vaginal bleeding and shortness of breath. History of systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, Factor V Leiden thrombophilia, and recurrent pregnancy losses. Currently on therapeutic anticoagulation (Warfarin 5mg daily), hydroxychloroquine, prednisone, and aspirin. Labs demonstrate markedly elevated hCG (450,000 mIU/mL) and hyperthyroidism (TSH <0.01, T4 3.2 ng/dL). Physical exam shows tachycardia (HR 110 bpm), diffusely enlarged thyroid, and slightly enlarged uterus with vaginal bleeding. Pelvic ultrasound shows enlarged uterus with heterogeneous, multicystic mass occupying the uterine cavity.
must_include_findings: Fetal pole and cardiac activity assessment
Uterine size relative to gestational age

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pulmonary embolism?
submission.pre_read_summary: 40-year-old female with history of pulmonary embolism (diagnosed January 2020) presenting with acute-onset shortness of breath, palpitations, lightheadedness, and anxiety that began an hour ago while walking up stairs. She is on combined oral contraceptives for 8 years, has a 20-pack-year smoking history, and recently returned from a 10-hour flight from South America. Vitals show tachycardia (HR 112/min), tachypnea (RR 28/min), and hypoxia (O2 sat 92% on room air). Elevated D-dimer and sinus tachycardia on ECG. Chest x-ray is normal with no infiltrates, effusion, or consolidation.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of traumatic injury to the abdomen and pelvis, including pelvic fractures, solid organ injuries, and retroperitoneal hemorrhage?
submission.pre_read_summary: 22M construction laborer with high-speed motor vehicle collision presenting with severe pelvic pain, hemodynamic instability (BP 90/60, HR 120), and physical findings of unstable pelvis with ecchymosis across lower abdomen and perineum. History of traumatic hemothorax with hypovolemic shock from January 2020. Hemoglobin 9 g/dL (down from baseline 14 g/dL). FAST exam negative for intra-abdominal fluid.
must_include_findings: free fluid in abdomen or pelvis

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of inflammatory breast cancer or other malignancy in the left breast?
submission.pre_read_summary: 47-year-old female presenting with 2-month history of progressive left breast pain and swelling. Physical examination reveals diffuse left breast enlargement, erythema, edema with peau d'orange appearance, nipple retraction, and palpable firm axillary lymph nodes. Laboratory studies demonstrate elevated ESR, CEA, and CA 15-3. Mammography shows skin thickening and increased breast density without distinct mass. Breast MRI reveals extensive non-mass enhancement with skin involvement and suspicious axillary lymphadenopathy. Patient has no family history of breast cancer. Social history includes current smoking (1 pack/week for 20 years).
must_include_findings: Skin involvement with thickening and edema

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pneumonia as the cause of the patient's altered mental status and hypoxia?
submission.pre_read_summary: 65M with Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer, severe COPD, and multiple comorbidities presenting with AMS, hypoxia (90% on room air), tachycardia (122/min), and hypotension (84/52). Physical exam shows decreased breath sounds in right lower lobe and crackles in both bases. Labs show leukocytosis (23,000), elevated lactate (4.5), and metabolic acidosis (pH 7.30, PaCO2 32, HCO3 15). Patient reports worsening productive cough for several days. Chest x-ray reveals large right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms.
must_include_findings: large right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of rupture of membranes and what is the status of the pregnancy?
submission.pre_read_summary: 28-year-old pregnant female presenting with 6-hour history of intermittent clear vaginal fluid leakage. Physical exam confirms pooling of clear fluid in vaginal vault. Nitrazine test positive with ferning on microscopy. Ultrasound shows amniotic fluid index of 3 cm with fetus in cephalic presentation and normal biophysical profile. Family history includes maternal history of PPROM.
must_include_findings: Fetus in cephalic presentation with normal biophysical profile
Pooling of clear fluid in vaginal vault on speculum exam
Nitrazine test positive with ferning on microscopy

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of emphysema/COPD progression or complications such as pneumothorax in a 34-year-old male with progressive dyspnea, wheezing, and chest x-ray findings of hyperlucency and bilateral basal bullous changes?
submission.pre_read_summary: 34-year-old male with 14-month history of progressively worsening shortness of breath and fatigue. Reports exertional dyspnea (winded walking up stairs), mild dry cough, and occasional wheezing. Works as high school coach. Partner resumed smoking over a year ago (secondhand smoke exposure). Vitals: O2 sat 91% on room air. Physical exam: scattered end-expiratory wheezes and bibasilar rhonchi. Chest x-ray shows hyperlucency and bilateral basal bullous changes. Pulmonary function tests demonstrate obstructive ventilatory pattern with decreased DLCO. No active problems or medications. Family history: father died at age 58 from liver failure.

submission.clinical_question: What is the cause of acute hypoxia in a 58-year-old female undergoing hip arthroplasty with intraoperative blood transfusion?
submission.pre_read_summary: 58-year-old female undergoing elective hip arthroplasty who developed acute dyspnea and hypoxia (O2 sat 81%) 45 minutes into intraoperative blood transfusion.
