Physical exam shows bilateral crackles without wheezing. Labs show normal immunoglobulin levels and negative Coombs test. Chest X-ray reveals bilateral pulmonary infiltrates without cardiomegaly or volume overload. Differential includes transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI), pulmonary embolism, and other causes of acute hypoxia.

submission.clinical_question: What is the cause of sudden onset severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding in a pregnant patient with history of chronic hypertension, ruptured ectopic pregnancy, and prior cesarean section?
submission.pre_read_summary: 33-year-old female at approximately 20-24 weeks gestation presenting with sudden onset of severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. History of chronic hypertension, ruptured ectopic pregnancy in May 2020 (treated with laparoscopic left salpingectomy), and placental abruption requiring emergency cesarean section. Current pregnancy with irregular and tachycardic fetal heart tones. Physical exam reveals tense, tender abdomen. Labs show mild anemia (Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL). Family history includes maternal aunt with ectopic pregnancy and paternal grandmother with DVT. Social history: current smoker (0.5 packs/day). Previous imaging shows retroplacental clot and decreased amniotic fluid volume.
must_include_findings: Presence of free fluid in pelvis

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of deep vein thrombosis in the left calf?
submission.pre_read_summary: 55-year-old male with history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, procainamide-induced systemic lupus erythematosus, and quadriceps tendon rupture, currently on warfarin therapy (INR 3.1). Presents with acute onset left calf swelling and mild pain for 2 days. Physical exam shows left lower extremity warm, erythematous, tender along posterior calf with mild pitting edema.
must_include_findings: Assessment of left lower extremity veins for thrombus
Evaluation for DVT in left calf
Assessment of venous flow and patency

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of interstitial lung disease (pulmonary fibrosis) as the cause of progressive dyspnea and cough?
submission.pre_read_summary: 55M with 30-pack-year smoking history and construction work presents with progressive exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough over 6 months. Physical exam reveals bilateral end-inspiratory crackles. Labs are unremarkable. Prior imaging shows diffuse interstitial infiltrates on CXR. Current HRCT demonstrates subpleural reticular changes and honeycombing without significant lymphadenopathy. Pulmonary function tests show restrictive pattern with reduced diffusion capacity. Active problems include hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Family history significant for CAD.
must_include_findings: bilateral end-inspiratory crackles on physical exam

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pheochromocytoma in the right adrenal mass and are there any features concerning for malignancy or invasion that would impact surgical planning?
submission.pre_read_summary: 45-year-old female with known pheochromocytoma (diagnosed 2020-01-15) presenting with paroxysmal hypertension episodes characterized by pounding headaches, palpitations, and diaphoresis occurring several times per week. Elevated plasma metanephrines and catecholamines confirm biochemical diagnosis. Family history suggestive of MEN 2A syndrome (father with medullary thyroid carcinoma, sister with pheochromocytoma). Currently scheduled for surgical resection of right adrenal mass. Preoperative CT abdomen to evaluate adrenal mass characteristics, assess for local invasion, and plan surgical approach.
must_include_findings: Size and location of right adrenal mass
Enhancement characteristics of the adrenal mass
Presence of calcifications within the mass
Invasion of adjacent structures (kidney, liver, IVC)

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of resolution of the lung abscess or any complications/recurrence?
submission.pre_read_summary: 65M with history of aspiration lung abscess (resolved) and ischemic stroke with persistent oropharyngeal dysphagia. Patient completed prolonged course of clindamycin for severe lung infection one year ago. Previous imaging revealed cavitary lesion in right lower lung field with air-fluid level. Current surveillance chest x-ray ordered for follow-up. Physical exam is unremarkable. Sputum cultures and inflammatory markers are negative.
must_include_findings: persistent rounded opacity in right lower lung field
comparison with prior imaging for resolution or progression

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of hiatal hernia or other esophageal pathology causing postprandial chest pressure and early satiety?
submission.pre_read_summary: 68-year-old female with history of hypertension, coronary artery disease, and GERD on PPI therapy presents with progressive shortness of breath and postprandial chest pressure with early satiety over the past 2 months. Denies dysphagia, odynophagia, or reflux symptoms. Physical exam unremarkable. Chest x-ray reveals air-fluid level in posterior mediastinum.
must_include_findings: herniation of gastric fundus above the diaphragm

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of an underlying vascular malformation (e.g., AVM, aneurysm) causing spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage in this 26-year-old female with thunderclap headache?
submission.pre_read_summary: 26-year-old female presents with sudden onset severe occipital headache, nausea, and vomiting while playing basketball. History of intermittent tension-type headaches. Family history significant for paternal uncle with cerebral arteriovenous malformation. Physical exam reveals right homonymous hemianopia. Non-contrast head CT demonstrates left occipital lobe hemorrhage without evidence of calcification or mass effect. Vitals stable (BP 130/85, HR 98, afebrile).
must_include_findings: no evidence of mass effect or midline shift

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of coarctation of the aorta?
submission.pre_read_summary: 15M with elevated blood pressure (150/90 mmHg) found at school health fair, history of headaches and dizziness for past year. Physical exam reveals weak/delayed femoral pulses compared to brachial pulses. Chest x-ray shows inferior rib notching of the third to eighth ribs.
must_include_findings: Inferior rib notching of the third to eighth ribs

submission.clinical_question: What is the etiology of the 8-cm right ovarian mass with solid and cystic components and calcification in this 12-year-old premenarchal female presenting with lower abdominal discomfort?
submission.pre_read_summary: 12-year-old female presenting with intermittent lower abdominal discomfort and feeling of fullness for 4 days. Premenarchal status with Tanner stage II breast and pubic hair development. Physical examination reveals a firm, non-tender right adnexal mass. Laboratory studies including beta-hCG and inflammatory markers are within normal limits. Previous imaging demonstrates an 8-cm right ovarian mass with solid and cystic components and areas of calcification. No ascites or evidence of metastatic disease.

Areas of calcification within the mass

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of new demyelinating lesions in the brain associated with a multiple sclerosis relapse causing the patient's visual symptoms?
submission.pre_read_summary: 30F with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (diagnosed 2020) presents with intermittent visual blurring in right eye, involuntary muscle spasms of left hand, and urinary urgency. Physical exam reveals hyperreflexia and clonus in left upper extremity, decreased sensation to vibration in right lower limb, subtle afferent pupillary defect on right, and mild optic disc swelling. Patient is on interferon beta-1a for MS treatment. Previous MRIs have shown multiple periventricular white matter lesions.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of postpartum urinary retention and what is the underlying cause?
submission.pre_read_summary: 27-year-old female, 8 hours post-spontaneous vaginal delivery, presents with inability to void and lower abdominal discomfort. Patient received epidural analgesia during labor. Physical exam reveals suprapubic fullness. Bladder scan demonstrates post-void residual volume of 600 mL, confirming significant urinary retention. Patient has history of anxiety disorder and is on fluoxetine. Prenatal course was unremarkable.
must_include_findings: presence of anechoic fluid within bladder

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of pulmonary histoplasmosis given the patient's cave exposure in the Mississippi River valley and radiographic findings of bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with reticulonodular infiltrates?
submission.pre_read_summary: 27-year-old male with primary sclerosing cholangitis, ulcerative colitis, and pemphigus vulgaris presents with 10 days of persistent fever, cough, and malaise following cave exploration in the Mississippi River valley. He returned 2 weeks ago from camping trip exploring caves and old barns. Physical exam shows scattered oral ulcers, tender cervical lymphadenopathy, decreased breath sounds with fine bibasilar crackles. Labs demonstrate mild normocytic anemia, elevated LDH, elevated CRP (24 mg/L), and elevated ESR (45 mm/hr). Chest radiograph reveals bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with patchy reticulonodular infiltrates. Sputum sent for fungal culture.

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of a malignant thyroid nodule in this 40-year-old female with a palpable neck mass?
submission.pre_read_summary: 40-year-old female presenting with a 2-cm firm, non-tender nodule in the right thyroid lobe discovered on self-examination. Physical exam shows no cervical lymphadenopathy. FNA cytology reveals deposits that stain with Congo red and demonstrate apple-green birefringence under polarized light, consistent with amyloid deposition. Patient has no family history of thyroid cancer or endocrine disorders. Currently on levothyroxine replacement therapy.
must_include_findings: 2-cm solid hypoechoic nodule in right thyroid lobe

submission.clinical_question: Is there evidence of aortic dissection?

Family history of AAA (mother had repair at age 72). Physical exam shows widened mediastinum on CXR, significant BP differential between arms (180/95 right vs 165/90 left), diastolic murmur at right second intercostal space, and weak femoral pulse compared to radial pulse. weak femoral pulse compared to radial pulse
